deities: Guru Padmasambhava (eight incarnations in fierce form depicted)
Zangdok Palri (Guru Rinpoche's heavenly palace) - seven-tiered painted wooden model on the top floor, built by the late Dungzin Rinpoche over five years
festivals: Chaam (monastic mask dance) - 28th and 29th day of the 12th Tibetan month (February/March) - the monastery's main annual festival

history.dynasty: Namgyal dynasty (Sikkimese monarchy); originally a small lhakhang enlarged during the reign of the third Chogyal Chakdor Namgyal, who was regarded as the third reincarnation of Lhatsun Chempo, Jigme Pawo
history.period: Early modern - planned, designed and founded by Lama Lhatsun Chempo in 1705; one of the oldest and premier monasteries of Sikkim
history.summary: CSV TOWN NOTE: the CSV town 'Geyzing' is approximate - Pemayangtse Monastery stands on a hilltop near Pelling in Gyalshing district (Geyzing is the district headquarters town, a few km away), and is commonly listed as the Pelling Monastery. Founded in 1705 by Lama Lhatsun Chempo (Lhatsun Namkha Jigme), one of the three lamas who consecrated the first Chogyal of Sikkim, it is one of the oldest and premier monasteries of Sikkim and the most famous in West Sikkim. Originally a small lhakhang, it was enlarged under the third Chogyal Chakdor Namgyal. The monastery follows the Nyingma Order of Tibetan Buddhism and heads all other Nyingma monasteries in Sikkim; its monks are normally chosen from Sikkim's Bhutia community and are the only ones entitled to the title 'ta-tshang' (pure monks - of pure Tibetan lineage, celibate, without physical abnormality). The head lama once had the privilege of anointing the Chogyals with holy water. 'Pemayangtse' means 'perfect sublime lotus', said to represent one of the four plexus of the human body. The three-storey Tibetan-style structure at about 2,100 m (6,840 ft) overlooks the Rabdentse ruins and houses idols, scriptures and murals; its crown jewel is the seven-tiered painted wooden Zangdok Palri model. It is part of the Buddhist pilgrimage circuit of Yuksom (Dubdi Monastery), Norbugang Chorten, Tashiding, Rabdentse, Sanga Choeling and Khecheopalri Lake. Religious affiliation verified as Nyingma Tibetan Buddhism - NOT a Hindu temple.

name: Pemayangtse Monastery
town_description: Pelling, at about 2,150 m in Gyalshing district of West Sikkim, is Sikkim's premier hill resort town with close views of Kanchenjunga. It lies about 130-140 km west of Gangtok (verify). Nearby attractions include the Pemayangtse Monastery, the ruins of Rabdentse (the old Sikkimese capital), Sanga Choeling Monastery, Khecheopalri Lake and Darap village.

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Bagdogra (IXB), approx. 130-160 km (verify); Pakyong Airport is closer but has limited flights.
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station is New Jalpaiguri (NJP), approx. 130-150 km (verify).
travel.road: About 2 km from the Upper Pelling football ground; reachable by taxi or shared jeep from Pelling or Geyzing (Gyalshing). A well-maintained garden compound within the monastery complex.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for clear Himalayan views; February-March for the Chaam dance festival (dates follow the Tibetan calendar).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Monastery visiting hours typically 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM (verify); entry ticket around Rs. 30-50 reported for similar West Sikkim sites (verify before visiting). Photography rules inside the shrine hall vary (verify).
